title: Phased fallback lattice and autonomous surge controller for safe upgrades
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design and implement an automated release gating system that composes phased fallbacks (a latticed set of holdback cohorts and progressive ramps) with an autonomous surge controller that clamps and redistributes traffic when instability signals or capacity spikes are detected. This ticket covers the runtime admission controller, the rollout policy primitives exposed in the Console/CLI, the feature-flag integration surface, and the auto-rollback decision engine tied to telemetry and quality signals.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime admits a new revision using a 4-stage lattice: shadow -> 1% canary -> adaptive ramp -> global promotion
Surge controller intervenes when combined signal score exceeds threshold and transparently shifts percentage to fallback variants within 30s
Auto-rollback triggers when p95 latency > X ms for 5m AND error-rate delta > 2x baseline OR quality-regression score exceeds configured threshold
Console exposes a single-tap pause/holdback and shows live safety-score breakdown (latency, errors, quality, infra) per cohort
End-to-end e2e simulation validates no more than 0.1% production traffic misrouted during a staged failure scenario
Docs and runbook for on-call and SRE included, plus one run of chaos test in staging
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff with Product and SRE; aligned on safety-score components and initial thresholds. Action: SRE to provide baseline telemetry buckets (latency, error, quality) by 2026-03-01.

2026-02-27: Prototype of lattice admission controller completed (local sim). Observed stable ramp behavior for evenly distributed request streams. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-orch/pull/312

2026-03-03: Design review with Console team. Decided to surface 'safety score' and an emergency 'circuit hold' in Console UI; Console will add toggle and cohort view (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASE/Phased+Fallback+Lattice+Design)

2026-03-07: Initial surge controller prototype implemented. Uses moving-window anomaly detector over weighted signals. Needs tuning for multi-tenant noisiness. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/surge-controller/pull/18

2026-03-09: Experiment plan approved: run lattice in shadow mode for two internal services (chat-generation, embeddings-indexing) for 2 weeks; collect safety-score distributions and false-positive rollback rate.

2026-03-10: Discovered an edge case where heterogeneous model variants (quantized vs float) bias quality-signal; engineering decision: add model-variant weighting to safety-score to avoid spurious rollbacks. Follow-up task created.

Next steps: integrate feature-flag SDK (LaunchDarkly/FF-as-code) to orchestrate cohort membership; finalize SLO-based thresholds and rollout policy DSL extension; schedule chaos runbook for 2026-03-24.
engineering_notes: Safety-score composition: 40% latency (p95), 30% infra errors (5xx/connection fails), 20% functional quality (eval prompt set), 10% SLO burn rate
Adaptive ramp heuristic: start at 1% for 10 minutes, evaluate safety-score; if score below low_threshold, increase to 5% for 15 minutes; apply exponential backoff on subsequent ramps if noise high

Surge controller policy: when aggregated signal > surge_threshold -> reduce new revision traffic by at least 50% and switch to nearest LTS-compatible variant; persist hold for min 5 minutes unless operator clears
Auto-rollback: must be reversible (retain previous revision KV cache) and execute safe-decrement (not all-or-nothing) to avoid traffic oscillation
Feature-flag integration: cohort membership will be derived from flag targeting rules, with ability to pin users/clients to holdback cohorts for experiments
Telemetry hooks: extend rollout telemetry with per-cohort token-level cost, model-variant id, and quality-eval sampling tag
risks: False-positive rollbacks due to noisy quality signals from small sample sizes
Incompatible rollback actions for stateful workflows (session affinity / long-lived KV caches)
Operational complexity: more knobs increases confusion for on-call if not surfaced clearly in Console
Multi-tenant interference when surge controller acts on noisy aggregated metrics
mitigations: Require minimum sample sizes and bootstrap priors for quality signals before gating decisions
Define rollback playbooks for stateful services and limit auto-rollback to stateless endpoints by default
Console design will include clear recommended defaults and a 'guided rollback' assistant for first-time operators
Surge controller to maintain tenant-aware baselines and only act on tenant-specific anomalies unless global failure detected
